Multivariate normality tests (Mardia, energy)

Source: R/mv_normality.r
ks_mv_normality.Rd

Mardia's skewness and kurtosis tests are implemented in base R (verified against `QuantPsyc::mult.norm`); the energy test (`energy::mvnorm.etest`) is attached automatically when the suggested energy package is installed, and silently skipped otherwise.

Usage

ks_mv_normality(x, R = 999, seed = NULL)

Arguments

x

A numeric matrix or data frame (rows = observations). `NA` rows are dropped.

R

Number of energy-test replicates.

seed

Integer seed for the energy permutation (reproducibility).

Value

A list with `mardia` (a `2 x 3` matrix: Beta-hat, kappa, p-val; `NULL` if the sample is too small), `energy` (or `NULL` when the energy package is missing), and `n`, `p`.

Details

Mardia: under multivariate normality, `A = n b1_p / 6` is chi-squared with `p(p+1)(p+2)/6` df, and the standardized `b2_p` is standard normal. The energy test is a consistent omnibus alternative; with `n < p + 2` Mardia's test is not defined and `NULL` is returned.

Examples

set.seed(0)
dat <- data.frame(x1 = rnorm(50), x2 = rnorm(50), x3 = rnorm(50))
out <- ks_mv_normality(dat)
out$mardia
#>           Beta-hat      kappa     p-val
#> Skewness  1.630474 13.5872843 0.1926626
#> Kurtosis 13.895364 -0.7130395 0.4758213
out$energy$statistic
#> E-statistic 
#>   0.9092327
